brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Hex bases stacked in one column at (0,0) on levels 0, 1 and 2 (piece:0,0,0 / 0,0,1 / 0,0,2 full).
Two classic drawers on level 0: drawer:0#1,0#cut (half-s base at 1,0,0, north key) and drawer:0#0,-1#cut (half-n base at 0,-1,0, south key).

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full-div3 (open 3-compartment full-depth tray) sits in the top cell (0,0,2). Only one bin is on the top storey; the top cell's upper face is left uncovered as an open tray.

finish.summary: Built a three-storey tower: a single column of hex bases at (0,0) across levels 0–2, with two classic drawers on the bottom storey (on half-base cut faces at (1,0,0) and (0,-1,0)) and one open three-compartment bin in the top cell. Caps closed the remaining open faces and joints were locked; check_build returns no issues and meshClash is clear. The top storey holds one bin only, and no props were added since the brief is about structure.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
